facts.text: The modulation period λ was varied among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm in approximately 1 μm-thick Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer coatings produced by RF magnetron sputtering.
Nanoindentation creep tests were performed at room temperature with a maximum load of 5 mN and loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s.
Each nanoindentation test used a 100 s hold and 20 s unloading, with indentation depth maintained at approximately one-tenth to one-seventh of the coating thickness.
Deposition was conducted for 1 h at about 5 × 10^-4 Pa base pressure and 0.3 Pa working pressure using 100 sccm Ar, 150 W on the HEA target, and alternating 0/30 W on the Al target.
M16 contained semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces with misfit dislocations, whereas M8 contained coherent interfaces with continuous atomic planes.
M32 and M80 were grain-boundary dominated because their modulation periods exceeded the approximately 20 nm grain diameter.
The semicoherent interfaces in M16 were interpreted to impede dislocation glide, produce dislocation pileups, and generate localized high stress.

The authors proposed that stress-induced interfacial amorphization in M16 lowers atomic-migration barriers and enables diffusion or interface slip, although amorphization was not directly established in this study.
The λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer exhibited the greatest room-temperature creep resistance relative to coherent-interface M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32 and M80.
M16 showed minimum stress exponents of 2.6, 1.5, and 2.3 at loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s, respectively, consistent with atomic-diffusion or interface-slip creep.
M8, M32, and M80 generally had creep stress exponents greater than 3 and were assigned predominantly dislocation-slip or dislocation-climb creep.

At 1 mN/s, creep displacement decreased from about 24 nm for M80 to 10 nm for M16 and then increased to 19 nm for M8; the corresponding steady-state rates were 5.7 × 10^-4, 3.1 × 10^-4, and 4.1 × 10^-4 s^-1.
